name: Night_Visibility_Gameplay
description: Sub-feature of Demo_Day_Night_Cycle: How darkness at night affects gameplay mechanics, exploration, and educational observations

questions.question: Does night enable educational observations that are invisible during the day?
questions.answer: Yes. Stars, bioluminescence, nocturnal animal sounds, and condensation (visible at dawn) are all night-specific observations. The env_education module can key observations to a 'is_night' flag.

questions.question: Can the player identify rocks by touch or sound at night if they cannot see them?
questions.answer: Not in v1. No tactile or audio-based rock identification exists. At night, the scanner tool should provide audio/UI feedback that compensates for darkness, but this is not yet implemented.

questions.question: Does night teach the player about human vision limitations vs. technology augmentation?
questions.answer: Not in v1. The player simply cannot see well at night. A future enhancement could provide night vision goggles or a scanner night mode that contrasts natural vs. augmented vision.

questions.question: Does the educational content differ between a clear night and a cloudy night?
questions.answer: Not in v1. Cloud cover affects star visibility visually but does not change educational observations. A future enhancement could compare clear vs. overcast night skies.

questions.question: What single screenshot of night gameplay would make Steam shoppers wishlist?
questions.answer: A canyon under starlight with visible rock strata silhouettes and a player scanner casting a small cone of light. One image that says 'exploration continues after dark.'

questions.question: How does night gameplay compare to Subnautica's night cycle?
questions.answer: Subnautica's night is dangerous (predators). Our night is educational (stars, temperature, different observations). The differentiator is that night is not just a hazard — it is a different classroom.

questions.question: Could 'night changes what you learn' be a compelling Steam description line?
questions.answer: Yes. 'The same canyon teaches different lessons at midnight than at noon. Come back at night and see what you missed.' That is a retention hook and a marketing line simultaneously.

questions.question: What would a journalist call the most innovative aspect of night gameplay?
questions.answer: That darkness does not block education — it changes it. Most games make night a nuisance. This game makes night a different experience with its own curriculum.

questions.question: Does moonlight or starlight provide enough illumination to navigate without artificial light?
questions.answer: Partially. UE5's sky light provides ambient illumination from the star sphere. On a clear night, players can see silhouettes and major terrain features but cannot read fine detail or distinguish rock types by color.

questions.question: Does the player character have a flashlight or headlamp that activates automatically at night?
questions.answer: Not in v1. No player light source exists. The player relies on starlight and the scanner tool's UI feedback. A flashlight is a recommended enhancement for v1.1.

questions.question: Are there nocturnal visual effects (bioluminescence, glowing minerals) that only appear at night?
questions.answer: Not in v1. Bioluminescent flora or glowing mineral veins are particle/VFX enhancements that would make night exploration visually rewarding. This is high-value future scope.

questions.question: Does fog or mist form in the canyon at night due to temperature drop?
questions.answer: Not in v1. Ground fog at dawn is a visual enhancement that would reinforce the temperature system (condensation from overnight cooling). The temperature curve provides the data; the fog VFX is a separate implementation.

questions.question: Can night visibility be implemented purely through UE5 lighting and post-processing?
questions.answer: Yes. UE5 exposure compensation, sky light intensity, and directional light brightness all handle night naturally. The engine's eye adaptation system automatically adjusts to darkness. No custom shaders needed.

questions.question: What is the minimum UE5 work to make night feel dark but playable?
questions.answer: Configure directional light intensity to approach 0 at night (not negative, just very dim). Set sky light to use the star sphere as its cubemap. Enable auto-exposure. Total: 3 blueprint nodes.

questions.question: Does night visibility have performance implications (more shadow resolve areas)?
questions.answer: Slightly. Dynamic shadow resolution does not increase at night, but the visible shadow cascade range remains the same. However, pure darkness can mask distant LOD transitions, potentially improving perceived quality.

questions.question: Can night be skipped or fast-forwarded for players who dislike darkness?
questions.answer: Yes. A 'wait until dawn' mechanic can be implemented as a UI button or campfire interaction. This respects player preference while preserving the system for those who engage with it.

questions.question: Can MCP verify that the player is in darkness by capturing and analyzing a viewport screenshot?
questions.answer: Yes. mcp_capture_viewport mode=editor_viewport returns a screenshot. Vision analysis can measure average pixel brightness to determine whether night has fallen. This enables automated night testing.

questions.question: Does the sleepwalker beat runner support night-specific expects (is_dark, star_visible)?
questions.answer: Not yet. The sleepwalker's expect vocabulary (13 actions, 19 expects) does not include light-level checks. A new expect like 'screen_darkness < 0.2' would need to be added to the sleepwalker's dispatch.

questions.question: Can educational observations at night be triggered independently of player line-of-sight?
questions.answer: Yes. If observations are proximity-triggered (entering a volume), the player does not need to see the object. The observation text can reference the darkness ('You hear water dripping — it must be condensation from the overnight temperature drop').

questions.question: What happens to the scanner tool at night — does it have a night mode?
questions.answer: Not in v1. The scanner tool has no night mode. A future enhancement could give the scanner a low-light amplification mode that reveals rock details the naked eye cannot see, teaching about technology augmentation.

questions.question: Does this depend on Celestial_Light_Rotation providing the darkness state?
questions.answer: Yes. Night is defined as the directional light being below the horizon (or below a brightness threshold). The celestial rotation system determines when it is night; this system defines what night means for gameplay.

questions.question: Does this depend on Temperature_Time_System for night-specific educational observations?
questions.answer: Yes. Night-specific educational content (cold-related geology facts, condensation, star identification) requires temperature data. The two systems combine to produce night-specific observations.

questions.question: Does this depend on the Demo_Educational_Triggers system for proximity-based night observations?
questions.answer: Yes. Night observations that fire when the player enters a trigger volume require the educational triggers system. The trigger volume checks time-of-day before deciding which observation to show.

questions.question: Does this prove that darkness can be a gameplay feature rather than a visual limitation?
questions.answer: Yes. By changing which educational observations are available at night, darkness becomes a design feature. Players have a reason to play at night (different content) rather than waiting for daylight.

questions.question: Does this prove that an educational game does not need constant visibility to teach?
questions.answer: Yes. Night teaches that science happens even when you cannot see clearly. Thermal expansion at night, condensation at dawn, star positions — these are real concepts that require darkness to understand.

questions.question: Was this derived from the Demo_Day_Night_Cycle surface design (how night affects gameplay and education)?
questions.answer: Yes. The parent feature asked 'Does day/night affect which educational observations appear?' This sub-feature answers that question in detail, defining the gameplay and educational consequences of darkness.
